## Where to write

The run directory is `/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure`. Write exactly `run_m4.py` and
`onbox_m4.sh` there, by absolute path. Write nothing anywhere else. Read the design record at
`/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure/out/design_record.json` and the conventions in `frozen/`
(provenance.py is the record writer; lambda_run.sh and remote_run.sh show what the box does). `lambda_run_m4.sh` and

## Checklist of gate changes the build must carry (37 entries)

1. **Order on the box.** install and downloads (with the smoke check, item 33); R1 controls (60 s sleep, empty run,
   unit-and-scale print); anchor (serial, then parallel); per-pair docking and analysis (aux timing); AlphaFold timings
   (seed-major); MD timings; storage; endpoints. A guard before every stage. (GATE_COMMIT answers 7, 14.)
2. **Files (rule 5).** The build writes exactly `run_m4.py` and `onbox_m4.sh` in
   `/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure` (absolute path), and reads the design record and
   `frozen/`. Payload shipped to the box: `run_m4.py onbox_m4.sh remote_run_m4.sh frozen/provenance.py`, and `data/` recursively
   if it exists, all under `~/m4_run/`. Results under `~/m4_run/results_m4/out/`, which the launcher fetches. Nothing else is on
   the box.
3. **Records (rule 6).** For each input C1 to C4 one provenance.py record `results_m4/out/endpoint-C<i>_tag-m4.json`; its `values`
   carries `measured` (a number in the card's unit: C1 h per run, C2 ns/day, C3 h per pair, C4 GiB), `unit`, `card_value`
   (0.5, 129, 1, 200) and `band` ([0.2, 1.25], [51.6, 322.5], [0.3333, 3], [66.67, 600]); its `decision` is PASS, FAIL or VOID
   against that band; `run_valid` in every record. An anchor record `endpoint-anchor_tag-m4.json` (values: `measured`,
   `published`, `tolerance`). `RUN_VALID.json`, `m4_summary.json`, and raw rows as JSON lines
   (`rows_<arm>_tag-m4.jsonl`, one line per timed run, per docking, per MD segment, per storage measurement). Records written
   before the anchor decision carry run_valid true; run_valid false propagates to every later record.
4. **Selftest (rule 7) (revised, addendum 3).** `python3 run_m4.py --selftest`: stdlib only, no GPU, no network, under 300 s;
   prints `selftest: N of M checks passed`, a line `selftest: files sha256 run_m4.py <hash> onbox_m4.sh <hash>` (item 36), then
   exactly `selftest: PASS` or `selftest: FAIL` as its last line; non-zero exit on FAIL. Planted cases for every parser and for
   the gate-failure (void) path (items 21 to 29 and 31 list them).
5. **Secrets (rule 8) (revised, addendum 3).** Nothing reads `.keys`; nothing prints its environment (no `env`, `printenv` or
   `set` dump; `env.txt` lists only named non-secret variables); `HF_TOKEN` is used by downloads only: `onbox_m4.sh` unsets
   `HF_TOKEN` and `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` after the downloads, and `run_tool` gives every child a copied environment with both
   removed. Selftest: a planted environment with both variables gives a child environment without them. (B7)
6. **Labels (rule 9) (revised, addendum 3).** Every measured record carries instance type (`INSTANCE_TYPE`), GPU name and driver
   (nvidia-smi), CUDA runtime version, engine version and build flags (AlphaFold implementation and its parameter archive hash,
   JAX build, docking code and version, MD engine, version, precision and platform, wheel or compiler build), start and end
   wall-clock, price per hour. Every C record also carries \"stand-in pairs built from 6IHB chains, not the card's pairs\", \"one
   GPU; one box; 3 pairs; no multi-GPU scaling\" and `n`. C1 adds \"no-MSA: alignment search time excluded; understates the
   card's setting\"; C2 the atom counts and engine precision; C3 \"producer's reading of aux hours\"; C4 \"linear in runs;
   intermediates kept; MD length 0.5 ns\". The anchor adds `independent_code: \"not run: single docking code\"`. Every record
   written after a guard, ceiling or timeout stop carries \"incomplete run: unmeasured inputs are VOID, not holding\" (item 35).
7. **Nothing interactive; downloads; command (rule 10) (revised, addendum 3).** No prompts anywhere; `sudo` only for declared
   apt packages (the build declares them in `onbox_m4.sh`), called as `sudo -n env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get ...`
   (B11); downloads only from the sources in item 14, URL and sha256 recorded for each (pip and apt too, item 34); the on-box
   command the build returns (`onbox_command`) is one line the operator runs verbatim through `remote_run_m4.sh`.
8. **Broken infrastructure (rule 4) (revised, addendum 3).** Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.8, driver 570, python 3.10, torch 2.7 are
   preinstalled; anything else is installed by `onbox_m4.sh` inside the time cap. Any failure of install, download, GPU check,
   smoke check (item 33) or tool start, and any real tool failure (non-zero exit, crash, missing output): exit non-zero with a
   void record (run_valid false, summary written, `RUN_DONE` with the exit code); never patch around, never substitute a tool or
   a source. A tool call that merely exceeds its stage allowance is not broken infrastructure: it is a ceiling stop (item 29).
   Exit codes: 2 infrastructure or harness failure, 3 cost or time guard stop, 4 anchor miss.
9. **Caps (rules 1, 2) (revised, addendum 3).** `onbox_m4.sh` reads `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR`, `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` and `REMOTE_TIMEOUT`
   from its environment, with no default that exceeds `BUDGET_LEFT_USD=5` or `REMOTE_TIMEOUT=7200`, and stops cleanly, writing a
   void record for unfinished work, before projected spend reaches `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` or elapsed time reaches `REMOTE_TIMEOUT`.
   Hard cap USD 10 for the run, at most two launches. It records the `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` it sees in `env.txt` and
   `m4_summary.json`; if unset it uses 7200 and labels \"REMOTE_TIMEOUT not forwarded; default 7200 used\" (item 37). (B4)
10. **Scope (rule 3).** Measure the inputs on the card's own protocol; no production phase, no 54-run pilot, no 216-run grid;
    anchor first; a missed anchor voids the inputs (run_valid false propagates to every later record).
11. **Gate scope (answer 1).** The card's gate (`af2_h_per_run <= 1`) is applied to C1 only: C1 values carry `gate_value`,
    `gate_pass` and the card's fallback text in `gate_else` (\"take the docking-plus-MD fallback line with one AlphaFold-Multimer
    seed per pair, or move the grid to 12 pairs\"); C2 and C3 carry `gate: \"not applicable: the card's gate is on
    af2_h_per_run\"`. The C1 decision is the band alone. The run does not branch on the gate.
12. **Pairs and seeds (answer 2).** 3 stand-in pairs built from chains of the 6IHB entry, one per capsid slot, each a
    hetero-multimer of 750 to 1,000 residues with the lengths spread over that range; chain ids, sequences, lengths and file
    hash recorded. AlphaFold seeds 0, 1, 2. Seed-major order. Minimums: C1 at least 3 completed runs covering all 3 pairs; C2
    at least 2 complexes (n recorded); C3 at least 2 pairs; C4 at least one run of each artifact type; below a minimum the
    record is VOID and the raw rows stay.
13. **AlphaFold protocol (answer 3).** One GPU; 5 models; exactly 20 recycles with early stopping off; single-sequence input
    only; no sequence database download and no remote alignment service. Measured = mean wall-clock hours of the whole
    prediction call per run, first-model compile included (the decision value); rows also carry the compile-excluded figure when
    the log gives per-model times.
14. **Allowed download sources (answer 3).** The PDB entry 6IHB from RCSB; the AlphaFold parameter archive from the
    AlphaFold project's own storage address; Python wheels through pip and declared packages through apt. Each URL and sha256
    recorded. Any other host is not allowed; a failed download stops the run (item 8).
15. **Auxiliary hours (answer 4).** aux_h_per_pair = per pair wall-clock hours of docking, interface analysis (contacts at
    4.5 A, interface residues, distance to the nearest threefold axis, site class) and writing the call-table row; installs,
    downloads and setup excluded; mean over the finished pairs (3 if all finish). One pip-installable docking code, name and
    version recorded.
16. **Storage (answer 4).** n_storage_gib = apparent bytes written for one grid run (AlphaFold outputs of one run; docking
    poses and tables of one pair; MD trajectory and logs of one 0.5 ns segment, frame interval recorded), intermediates kept,
    x 216, / 2^30; the decision value. The record also carries the 432-run figure, the intermediates-deleted figure and MD bytes
    per ns, as information.
17. **MD protocol (answers 5, 10).** One docked complex per sampled pair (the top docking pose of that pair), explicit solvent,
    water padding chosen so the atom count is inside 120,000 to 180,000; minimise, short equilibration, then a 0.5 ns
    production segment; one velocity seed (0). ns/day from the engine's rate line and, separately, from production steps x
    timestep over the wall-clock of the production segment; the decision value is the median over complexes of the wall-clock
    figure; if the two disagree by more than 5 percent every ns/day is labelled \"engine rate and wall-clock disagree\" and both
    are reported. Atom count outside the range: C2 VOID.
18. **Marginal rule (GATE_COMMIT instrument queue).** A value within 10 percent of a band edge (`edge x 0.9` to `edge x 1.1`) is
    decision VOID with `marginal: true`; the raw value is kept in `measured`.
19. **Non-A100 GPU (design, does_not_test).** If the GPU is not an A100 (instance fallback), C1 and C2 are VOID with the raw
    number kept and the label \"not an A100\"; C3 and C4 are still decided and labelled with the GPU.
20. **Controls first (answer 7).** After install: planted 60 s sleep (error at most 5 percent, else run_valid false, exit 2);
    empty-input run (time under 2 s and bytes under 1 MiB, else the excess is subtracted from later values and the label
    \"setup overhead subtracted\"); one unit-and-scale record (raw AlphaFold seconds, MD rate lines with the wall-clock ns/day
    beside them, raw bytes per artifact). No band is compared before these are written.
21. **Anchor readout (answer 8; revised, addendum 3).** Contact overlap = fraction of 6IHB interface residue-residue contacts
    (heavy-atom pair at most 4.5 A) that the pose makes; pass if overlap at least 0.50 or interface backbone RMSD at most 5.0 A,
    and serial vs parallel top-pose RMSD at most 2.0 A with identical bind/no-bind calls. Selftest, planted: (0.50, RMSD 9.0)
    pass; (0.49, 5.0) pass; (0.49, 5.01) fail; serial-parallel 2.0 with equal calls pass, 2.01 fail, 0.0 with different calls
    fail; 3 of 6 contacts gives 0.5; a 5.0 A shift along x gives RMSD 5.0. The anchor runs serially, then in parallel on the
    same box, seed 0. A miss writes C1 to C4 as VOID, run_valid false, exit 4. The second independent docking code is not run
    (answer 5). Added by addendum 3: (a) contacts are keyed by chain role, not by the file's chain id: the reference and the
    pose pass through one chain-mapping function before keys are built, so the same planted pose gives overlap 0.5 with the
    receptor chain id \"B\", \"C\" and \"A\", and an overlap of 0.0 on a planted pose with non-trivial overlap fails the selftest,
    native-versus-pose round trip through `write_pdb` and `read_pdb_atoms` included (B5); (b) the interface backbone RMSD is over
    the N, CA, C, O atoms of the receptor residues that form the reference interface (any heavy atom within 4.5 A of the capsid
    in 6IHB), in the capsid frame, no superposition; a planted pose moving only non-interface receptor atoms by 20 A gives
    interface RMSD 0.0000 and a whole-chain RMSD above 0; the serial-parallel RMSD stays over the whole receptor chain and is
    labelled so (B10).
22. **C1 selftest (answer 9).** 1,800 s per run gives 0.5 h; means 0.5 PASS, 1.5 FAIL, 0.1 FAIL, 1.2 VOID, 0.21 VOID, 1.1 PASS
    with `gate_pass` false and the fallback text, 0.9 PASS with `gate_pass` true; n=2 runs VOID; 3 runs missing one pair VOID.
23. **C2 selftest (answer 10).** A planted engine log rate line parses to its number; 250,000 steps x 2 fs in 335 s gives 128.96
    ns/day; median of (100, 129, 500) is 129 PASS; 40 FAIL; 400 FAIL; 56 VOID; 60 PASS; 330 VOID; atom counts 119,999 and
    180,001 VOID, 150,000 passes the size check; a GPU name other than A100 VOID for C1 and C2.
24. **C3 selftest (answer 11).** Three pair wall-clocks of 3,600 s give 1.0 h PASS; 0.2 FAIL; 4.0 FAIL; 0.3333 VOID; 3.2 VOID;
    0.5 PASS; 2.5 PASS; 7,200 s install plus 1,800 s docking gives 0.5 h.
25. **C4 selftest (answer 12).** 1,073,741,824 bytes per run = 1.0 GiB x 216 = 216.0 PASS (432-run figure 432.0); 0.1 gives 21.6
    FAIL; 4.0 gives 864.0 FAIL; 2.9 gives 626.4 VOID; 0.35 gives 75.6 PASS; files of 1,000 and 24 bytes sum to 1,024.
26. **Harness selftest (answer 13).** 62.9 s for the 60 s sleep passes; 63.1 s fails (run_valid false, exit 2); timings (1,800,
    1,830, 1,790) pass the spread check; (1,800, 1,800, 1,800) fails and gives C1 VOID with \"zero spread across seeds: wrong
    variance source\" while other inputs stand; relative SD 0.6 gives the label \"seed spread high; mean is uncertain\" only;
    empty run 0.5 s and 100 KiB pass, 5 s or 2 MiB trigger the subtraction label.
27. **Cost and time selftest (answer 14; revised, addendum 3).** 3,600 s at 1.99 gives 1.99; 7,200 s gives 3.98; with price
    1.99, budget 5, timeout 7,200 the guard stops at the time cap (5 / 1.99 h = 9,045 s is above it); with price 2.50 both caps
    coincide at 7,200 s; with 3.00 the dollar cap stops at 6,000 s; a stage whose estimated remaining time exceeds the time left
    is not started, the guard writes VOID (unmeasured) records for unfinished inputs, keeps finished ones, exits 3, and leaves
    run_valid as it was. The gate-failure (void) path is also planted for: anchor miss, sleep failure, install failure,
    download failure, smoke-check failure. The stage flow itself (not only the functions) is planted in item 31.
28. **Stage ceilings (GATE_COMMIT answer B8; revised, addendum 3).** In seconds: install and downloads with the smoke check
    1,800; controls and anchor 700; per-pair docking and analysis 600 in total, at most 250 per pair; AlphaFold 2,000; MD 1,600,
    at most 600 per complex; endpoints 100; margin 400; total 7,200. A stage's allowance is the lesser of its ceiling and the
    time left minus the margin and the endpoints slot. A stage that hits its ceiling stops and its unfinished inputs are VOID
    (\"unmeasured, not holding\", with the full incomplete-run label, item 35). A docking pair that reaches its 250 s is kept as a
    row with `truncated: true`, not counted in the mean; C3 stays decided if at least 2 pairs finished, else VOID.
29. **Gate-failure and guard-stop paths (answers 8, 13, 14; revised, addendum 3).** run_valid false when the anchor misses (exit
    4), the sleep check fails (exit 2), or infrastructure breaks (exit 2); it propagates to every later record, `RUN_VALID.json`
    and `m4_summary.json`. A guard stop does NOT set it false: a time-guard refusal to start a stage, a stage ceiling, a tool call
    exceeding its stage allowance, or the outer timeout (rc 124) voids the unfinished inputs, keeps finished inputs' decisions,
    leaves run_valid as it was, labels later records \"incomplete run: ...\", and the run ends with exit 3. `fail_stage` sets
    run_valid false only for exit 2 and 4. Each early return in `stage_af2`, `stage_aux` and `stage_md` raises `GuardStop` or
    records the stop in run state that `run_stages` reads; the stage is then not in `stages_done`; later stages whose own guard
    allows still start; `stage_endpoints` always runs; the final exit code is 3 whenever any input is unmeasured because of a
    guard, ceiling or timeout stop, and 0 only when every input was decided by measurement (a marginal VOID is a measured
    decision). A timed-out tool's row is kept with `incomplete: true` and is not counted in a mean. (B1, B2, B3)
30. **Summary and spread (answers 5, 6; revised, addendum 3).** `m4_summary.json` states first that the run decides the stand-in
    protocol only; restates every record, the gate result and the fallback text; carries no decision of its own; carries the
    label \"seed spread high; mean is uncertain\" for any pair with relative SD over 50 percent; and carries the full \"incomplete
    run\" label after an early stop. No relaunch is made for spread.
31. **Stage-flow selftest (new, addendum 3, B15).** `run_stages` takes its stage functions and tool runner by injection; the
    selftest runs the whole flow with fakes and asserts exit code, run_valid, per-input decisions and labels for: (a) all stages
    finish: exit 0, run_valid true; (b) a time-guard stop in AlphaFold after 2 of 9 runs: exit 3, run_valid true, C1 VOID with
    raw rows kept, C2 to C4 decided; (c) a tool timeout in MD on the third complex: exit 3, run_valid true, C2 decided on n=2,
    others untouched; (d) a ceiling stop in docking: exit 3, C3 decided on the finished pairs or VOID below 2; (e) a real tool
    failure: exit 2, run_valid false, all inputs VOID; (f) anchor miss: exit 4, run_valid false, C1 to C4 VOID; (g) sleep
    failure: exit 2; (h) install, smoke-check and download failure: exit 2; (i) the outer-timeout route (rc 124): exit 3,
    run_valid true.
32. **Process groups and outer timeout (new, addendum 3, B12).** Every tool call (colabfold, the docking code, the OpenMM
    worker) runs in its own process group and a timeout kills the group; when the outer `timeout` on `run_m4.py` returns 124,
    `onbox_m4.sh` kills the recorded process groups (by group id, not by name) before the endpoints stage and routes the
    outcome as a guard stop, exit 3, not as `fail`/exit 2. The inner tool timeout is at least 100 s shorter than the outer kill
    (outer kill = stop_at minus elapsed minus 600; inner = stop_at minus elapsed minus 700) so the inner fires first; an outer
    firing is itself a recorded event. Selftest: a planted tool that sleeps past its allowance is killed with its child and the
    result is a ceiling stop.
33. **Smoke check in the install stage (new, addendum 3, B6).** After every install and inside the 1,800 s install ceiling: import
    of the AlphaFold-Multimer stack and JAX with a GPU device listed; `colabfold_batch --help`; the docking code's entry point
    `--help`; OpenMM imported with `Platform.getPlatformByName(\"CUDA\")` succeeding. A failure is exit 2 with a void record before
    any GPU stage. Every package is pinned by version in the install line; the build chooses the package form that carries the
    CUDA platform for OpenMM and a JAX build compatible with the pinned `colabfold`, without substituting a tool; install order
    such that `colabfold_batch` still imports; the smoke check decides, not recollection.
34. **Downloads recorded in full (new, addendum 3, B13).** pip installs run with `--report`; the report (URL and archive hash of
    each wheel) is kept under `results_m4/out/` and its sha256 is cited in the records' `inputs`; each apt package is recorded
    with version and the SHA256 from `apt-cache show`; the direct downloads keep URL and sha256.
35. **Incomplete-run label (new, addendum 3, B9).** The constant \"incomplete run: unmeasured inputs are VOID, not holding\" exists
    beside `LABEL_UNMEASURED = \"unmeasured, not holding\"`; every record and the summary written after a guard, ceiling or
    timeout stop carries the full label. Selftest: a planted early-stopped run's records all contain it.
36. **Selftest ties its log to the files (new, addendum 3, B14).** The selftest prints
    `selftest: files sha256 run_m4.py <hash> onbox_m4.sh <hash>` (the script hashes itself and `onbox_m4.sh` with the stdlib)
    before its final line; the build's return states the real line counts and those hashes. The operator re-runs the selftest
    after the build and compares before any launch.
37. **Launcher and REMOTE_TIMEOUT (new, addendum 3, B4; operator's change, listed so the build relies on it).** `lambda_run_m4.sh`
    forwards `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` with `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR`, `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` and `INSTANCE_TYPE`; the build does not write it. The
    build's two files read the variable, never default above 7200, record the value seen (item 9), and label an unset value.

## Box

- Instance: `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4` (A100 SXM4 40 GB, USD 1.99/h) in us-east-1 if it has capacity; else the cheapest single GPU
  with capacity at no more than USD 2.50/h; the operator records which.
- Launcher (revised, addendum 3): the operator's per-launch copy `lambda_run_m4.sh` (made from `frozen/lambda_run.sh` at the
  header's declared points only; the header declares four added variables): remote dir `m4_run/`; payload `run_m4.py
  onbox_m4.sh remote_run_m4.sh frozen/provenance.py` and `data/` recursively if it exists; forwarded env `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR
  BUDGET_LEFT_USD REMOTE_TIMEOUT INSTANCE_TYPE` (build 2's copy omitted `REMOTE_TIMEOUT`; the operator fixes it before launch 1);
  fetch from `m4_run/results_m4/out/`. `remote_run_m4.sh` is `frozen/remote_run.sh` with only its `cd` line changed to
  `~/m4_run`.
- Caps: `REMOTE_TIMEOUT=7200`; `BUDGET_LEFT_USD=5` per launch; two launches at most within USD 10.
- Payload layout on the box: `~/m4_run/run_m4.py`, `~/m4_run/onbox_m4.sh`, `~/m4_run/frozen/provenance.py`, `~/m4_run/data/...`
  if shipped. Results under `~/m4_run/results_m4/out/`.
- The build's `onbox_command` is a single line the operator runs verbatim on the box through `remote_run_m4.sh`.

## Local selftest (revised, addendum 3)

`python3 run_m4.py --selftest` is stdlib-only and runs under `timeout 300`: no GPU, no network. It covers every parser
(engine rate line, MD log and production wall-clock, AlphaFold timing rows, docking and contact tables, byte counts, nvidia-smi
labels, pip report), the marginal rule, the planted cases of items 21 to 27, the stage-flow cases of item 31, the process-group
kill of item 32, the child-environment case of item 5, the incomplete-run label of item 35, the void path of item 29, record
writing through `frozen/provenance.py`, and the file-hash line of item 36. No local tool run (no AlphaFold, docking or MD).

## What the runner writes (`results_m4/out/`) (revised, addendum 3)

- `endpoint-anchor_tag-m4.json` and `endpoint-C1_tag-m4.json` to `endpoint-C4_tag-m4.json`, plus one provenance.py record
  for each control (60 s sleep, empty run, unit-and-scale), each with `cell`, `inputs` with hashes, `metric`, `values`,
  `threshold`, `decision_rule` written before values, `decision`, `run_valid`.
- Raw rows, one JSON line each (`rows_<arm>_tag-m4.jsonl`): every AlphaFold run (pair, seed, wall-clock, per-model times when
  available, `incomplete` when timed out), every docking and analysis timing (`truncated` when it hit its per-pair cap), every MD
  segment (complex, atom count, steps, wall-clock, engine rate), every storage measurement (artifact, apparent bytes).
- `RUN_VALID.json`; `env.txt` (named non-secret variables only, including the `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` seen); `m4_summary.json`; download,
  install, smoke-check and tool logs; the pip report and the apt package hashes (item 34); the `RUN_DONE` marker with the exit
  code (3 after any guard, ceiling or timeout stop with inputs unmeasured).

WRITE EXACTLY TWO NEW FILES in this repo and edit nothing existing:
run_m4.py - stages extract / generate / endpoints, runnable independently. Save every generation or measurement verbatim per row. Every result record carries a run_valid field; any gate or anchor endpoint that fails writes run_valid=false into EVERY record written after it, per-cell files included, never only a summary - a void that lives in one file is not a void. A --selftest that is stdlib-only (guard heavy imports) covering every parser, every degenerate-output detector, and each endpoint's arithmetic on planted rows with known decisions, including a planted gate-failure row that must propagate run_valid=false, and, where the design contains a dispersion rule, a planted zero-dispersion case that must halt WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE. 1: """Self-describing result artifacts: one home per fact.
2: 
3: WHY. A number that is typed into prose drifts from the run that produced it, and
4: nothing re-checks the pairing. The observed failure modes in the sibling projects
5: are: a summary number with no artifact behind it, a filename that disagrees with
6: its contents, and a coverage table maintained by hand so that missing cells are
7: invisible. All three are the same bug -- a fact living somewhere other than its
8: producer.
9: 
10: So: every run writes ONE json that carries its own identity, the inputs it was
11: computed from, and its own decision. Write-ups index into these by (cell, metric)
12: and resolve the value at read time; they do not restate it. `index.py` reads the
13: tree and answers "what has been run, over what inputs, with what result".
14: 
15: WHAT A RECORD CARRIES
16:   cell     identity of the run (model, variant, stage, arm, ...). The same dict
17:            the coverage grid is declared over, so present-vs-missing is a set
18:            difference rather than a hand-tally.
19:   inputs   every file the result was computed from, each with a content hash and
20:            an item count. `triage-reader` reads BOTH sides; this is the input
21:            side, recorded at write time because it cannot be reconstructed later.
22:   metric / values / threshold / decision_rule / decision
23:            the measurement and the neutral call on it, stated in terms of the
24:            measurement only.
25:   env      code revision, timestamp, host -- so a record can be told from a
26:            re-run of the same cell.
27: 
28: The decision rule is written BEFORE the values are known (it is an argument, not
29: a computation over `values`), which is what makes the refuting outcome nameable
30: in the artifact rather than in someone's memory.
31: 
32:     python provenance.py --selftest      # model-free, no GPU
33: """
34: 
35: from __future__ import annotations
36: 
37: import hashlib
38: import json
39: import platform
40: import socket
41: import subprocess
42: import sys
43: from datetime import datetime, timezone
44: from pathlib import Path
45: 
46: 
47: def _sha(path: Path, n: int = 12) -> str:
48:     h = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
49:     return h[:n]
50: 
51: 
52: def describe_input(path: str | Path, n_items: int | None = None) -> dict:
53:     """One input file: what it is, what it hashed to, how many items it held.
54: 
55:     n_items is supplied by the caller because only the caller knows how the file
56:     is parsed (lines, rows, records). Recording it here is the difference between
57:     an auditable input and a path that may since have changed under the result.
58:     """
59:     p = Path(path)
60:     if not p.exists():
61:         return {"path": str(p), "present": False, "sha256": None, "n_items": n_items}
62:     return {
63:         "path": str(p),
64:         "present": True,
65:         "sha256": _sha(p),
66:         "bytes": p.stat().st_size,
67:         "n_items": n_items,
68:     }
69: 
70: 
71: def _env(code_dir: str | Path = ".") -> dict:
72:     try:
73:         rev = subprocess.run(
74:             ["git", "-C", str(code_dir), "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
75:             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
76:         ).stdout.strip() or None
77:     except Exception:
78:         rev = None
79:     return {
80:         "git_rev": rev,
81:         "timestamp_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
82:         "host": socket.gethostname(),
83:         "python": platform.python_version(),
84:     }
85: 
86: 
87: def write_result(
88:     out_path: str | Path,
89:     *,
90:     cell: dict,
91:     inputs: list[dict],
92:     metric: str,
93:     values: dict,
94:     threshold: dict | None = None,
95:     decision_rule: str = "",
96:     decision: str = "",
97:     notes: str = "",
98:     rows: list | None = None,
99: ) -> Path:
100:     """Write one self-describing record. Returns the path written.
101: 
102:     `cell` must be flat and JSON-scalar valued: it is the join key against the
103:     coverage grid, and `index.py` asserts it against the path it was found at.
104:     """
105:     bad = {k: v for k, v in cell.items() if not isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool, type(None)))}
106:     if bad:
107:         raise ValueError(f"cell values must be JSON scalars; got {bad}")
108:     if not decision_rule:
109:         raise ValueError("decision_rule is required: state it before the values are known")
110: 
111:     rec = {
112:         "cell": cell,
113:         "inputs": inputs,
114:         "metric": metric,
115:         "values": values,
116:         "threshold": threshold or {},
117:         "decision_rule": decision_rule,
118:         "decision": decision,
119:         "notes": notes,
120:         "env": _env(Path(__file__).parent),
121:     }
122:     # The per-item outputs the summary was computed from. Kept in the same record
123:     # so a label can be re-derived from raw by its stated meaning, rather than by
124:     # re-running the scorer that produced it.
125:     if rows is not None:
126:         rec["rows"] = rows
127:     out = Path(out_path)
128:     out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
129:     out.write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
130:     return out
131: 
132: 
133: def cell_slug(cell: dict) -> str:
134:     """Filename-safe identity, so the path and the contents cannot disagree
135:     silently. `index.py` re-derives this and compares against the actual name."""
136:     parts = [f"{k}-{cell[k]}" for k in sorted(cell) if cell[k] is not None]
137:     slug = "_".join(parts)
138:     return "".join(c if (c.isalnum() or c in "-_.") else "-" for c in slug)
139: 
140: 
141: def _selftest() -> int:
142:     import tempfile
143: 
144:     fails = []
145:     with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
146:         d = Path(d)
147:         src = d / "items.jsonl"
148:         src.write_text('{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n')
149: 
150:         inp = describe_input(src, n_items=2)
151:         if not (inp["present"] and inp["n_items"] == 2 and len(inp["sha256"]) == 12):
152:             fails.append(f"describe_input: {inp}")
153:         if describe_input(d / "nope.json")["present"]:
154:             fails.append("missing input reported present")
155: 
156:         cell = {"model": "gemma-2-9b", "variant": "it", "stage": 1}
157:         slug = cell_slug(cell)
158:         if slug != "model-gemma-2-9b_stage-1_variant-it":
159:             fails.append(f"cell_slug: {slug}")
160: 
161:         p = write_result(
162:             d / f"{slug}.json", cell=cell, inputs=[inp], metric="flip_rate",
163:             values={"flip_rate": 0.42, "n": 74},
164:             threshold={"floor": 0.10, "ceiling": 0.90},
165:             decision_rule="flip_rate outside [0.10, 0.90] -> CEILING_OR_FLOOR, else IN_BAND",
166:             decision="IN_BAND",
167:         )
168:         rec = json.loads(p.read_text())
169:         for k in ("cell", "inputs", "metric", "values", "threshold", "decision_rule", "decision", "env"):
170:             if k not in rec:
171:                 fails.append(f"missing key {k}")
172:         if rec["env"]["timestamp_utc"][:2] != "20":
173:             fails.append("timestamp not populated")
174: 
175:         try:
176:             write_result(d / "x.json", cell=cell, inputs=[], metric="m", values={},
177:                          decision_rule="")
178:             fails.append("empty decision_rule accepted")
179:         except ValueError:
180:             pass
181:         try:
182:             write_result(d / "y.json", cell={"bad": [1, 2]}, inputs=[], metric="m",
183:                          values={}, decision_rule="r")
184:             fails.append("non-scalar cell accepted")
185:         except ValueError:
186:             pass
187: 
188:     for f in fails:
189:         print(f"FAIL {f}")
190:     print("selftest:", "PASS" if not fails else f"{len(fails)} FAILURES")
191:     return 1 if fails else 0
192: 
193: 
194: if __name__ == "__main__":
195:     if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
196:         sys.exit(_selftest())
197:     print(__doc__)

1: # On-box execution contract (seed for the launcher writer)
2: 
3: What the execution layer of a measure run must look like, as requirements and a schema, not code. The build agent
4: reads this beside the design record and the execution directive; the gate's directive may tighten any item, never
5: loosen one. Every item below exists because a run failed without it (m1 to m4, 2026-10; the frozen launcher's own
6: billing incidents, 2026-06 to 2026-08). Where an item names a number, the number is a floor or a ceiling, not a
7: suggestion.
8: 
9: ## 1. Shape
10: 
11: Two files, nothing else: `run_<tag>.py` (stages, parsers, records, selftest; stdlib only unless the design names a
12: library, and then only inside the on-box stages) and `onbox_<tag>.sh` (environment, order of stages, guards, exit
13: codes). The local launcher (`lambda_run_<tag>.sh`, operator-owned, never written by the build) ships the payload,
14: starts `remote_run_<tag>.sh bash onbox_<tag>.sh` detached under `timeout REMOTE_TIMEOUT`, polls a marker, fetches
15: `results_<tag>/out/` and terminates the box. The build never edits the launcher; if the launcher must change, the
16: build stops and reports the exact declared point.
17: 
18: ## 2. Interface
19: 
20: Environment in (every one optional, every one read through a default and echoed once into the environment record,
21: never dumped wholesale): `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR`, `BUDGET_LEFT_USD`, `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (seconds, the whole box
22: lifetime the launcher enforces), `INSTANCE_TYPE`, `LAMBDA_INSTANCE_ID`, `GIT_COMMIT`, `HF_TOKEN` (downloads only).
23: Files in: the payload under `~/<tag>_run/` exactly as listed in the directive; `data/` if shipped. Files out:
24: everything under `~/<tag>_run/results_<tag>/out/`; nothing written anywhere else on the box except the engine build
25: directories the directive names. Exit codes of `onbox_<tag>.sh`: 0 every stage done and valid; 2 infrastructure
26: (install, compile, download, GPU not visible); 3 guard stop (time or cost); 4 anchor failed; 5 a stage failed after
27: the anchor. The launcher records the code in `RUN_DONE`; the script never writes that file.
28: 
29: ## 3. Order of stages, each a hard gate for the next
30: 
31: 1. **Preflight** (seconds): GPU visible and named (`nvidia-smi`), driver and CUDA versions, free disk, python and
32:    the preinstalled libraries' versions, clock; all into `env_<tag>.json`. Any missing requirement: exit 2 at once.
33: 2. **Install or compile** from the sources the directive names, pinned by version or commit, hash of every
34:    downloaded archive recorded; non-interactive (`DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, `apt-get -y`, `pip -q`); wait
35:    for the apt lock rather than fail on it; never patch the source, never substitute a package: failure is exit 2.
36: 3. **Engine capability check** before any physics: query the built binary for the features the design relies on
37:    (package list, precision, styles, device) and compare with the directive's list; a missing feature is exit 2,
38:    never a fallback. This is the m3 lesson (a pinned build with the GPU package off ran two builds before anyone asked
39:    the binary).
40: 4. **Timed dry run** on the real input and the real command line, short (1 to 2 % of the main phase), measuring the
41:    rate the whole plan depends on; from it, project every remaining phase's wall-clock and cost.
42: 5. **Guard decision**, written as a record before the long phases: allowed seconds =
43:    `REMOTE_TIMEOUT - elapsed - fetch_margin(600 s)`; allowed cost = `BUDGET_LEFT_USD`; projected seconds from the
44:    measured rate with a 1.5x margin; if either projection exceeds its allowance, shorten per the directive's stated
45:    rule or stop with exit 3; the record carries every number of the arithmetic so a reader can redo it.
46: 6. **Anchor** (the published value the protocol must reproduce) before the inputs; a miss outside its tolerance
47:    writes the anchor record with decision FAIL, sets `run_valid=false` for every later record, and continues only if
48:    the directive says the inputs are still worth measuring (default: stop, exit 4).
49: 7. **Measurement phases** in the directive's order; each writes its record the moment it finishes (atomic: write a
50:    temp file, rename), never at the end of the run, so a killed run keeps every finished result.
51: 8. **Summary** last (`<tag>_summary.json`), then `RUN_VALID.json`; then exit.
52: 
53: ## 4. Guards
54: 
55: A guard reads only measured quantities: the dry run's rate, the clock, the price. It never trusts the card's or the
56: design's number for a rate. It re-checks before every long phase, not once. It stops cleanly: the current phase's
57: partial output is kept and labelled partial; the guard record states which phases did not run and why. Time cap
58: arithmetic uses the launcher's `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` from the environment, never a constant copied into the script.
59: 
60: ## 5. Records (provenance.py)
61: 
62: One record per endpoint, control and phase; the decision rule in the record before the values; `cell`, `inputs`
63: with hashes, `metric`, `values`, `threshold`, `decision`, `env`, `run_valid`, `run_valid_voided_by`. The inputs the
64: card is measured on: `endpoint-C<i>_tag-<tag>.json` with `values.measured` (a number, the card's unit), `values.unit`,
65: `values.card_value`, `values.band`; `decision` PASS, FAIL or VOID against the band. Labels in every measured record:
66: instance type, GPU name and driver, engine version and build flags, precision, wall-clock, process and thread counts
67: (a per-GPU rate on one process with the GPU idle is a different quantity from a per-GPU rate; m3 measured the former
68: and the card meant the latter). Raw rows (every run, every thermo or step line) as JSON lines beside the records.
69: Units in field names or in `values.unit`, never implied.
70: 
71: ## 6. Logging
72: 
73: All stdout and stderr of every stage into files under `results_<tag>/out/`; one short progress line per minute or per
74: phase to the main log so the launcher's one-line poll shows movement (a silent hour reads as a hang). No secrets, no
75: `env` dumps, no token in any log. Keep every engine log; keep the first and last lines of large sampling files, not
76: the whole.
77: 
78: ## 7. Selftest contract
79: 
80: `python3 run_<tag>.py --selftest`: stdlib only, no GPU, no network, under 300 s; planted cases for every parser (a
81: real-looking output line and a malformed one), for the guard arithmetic (a case that must stop and one that must go),
82: for the anchor miss (void propagation to a later record), for record writing through provenance.py, and for the
83: directive's own numbers (if two items of the directive disagree, the selftest fails on that contradiction rather than
84: picking one). Output: `selftest: N of M checks passed` then exactly `selftest: PASS` or `selftest: FAIL`, non-zero
85: exit on FAIL.
86: 
87: ## 8. Predictable failures and the check that catches each before money is spent
88: 
89: | failure (seen) | check in the build |
90: |---|---|
91: | engine built without the feature the design uses (m3 build 2) | stage 3 capability query against the directive's feature list |
92: | GPU style incompatible with a deck line (m3 launch 2) | dry run on the real deck and command line, not a toy input |
93: | main phase longer than the window (m3 launch 1) | stage 4 rate, stage 5 projection with margin, re-check per phase |
94: | labels or constants copied from the card and stale (m3 build 3) | labels read from runtime queries, never literals |
95: | rate measured on an idle GPU (m3 result) | process and thread counts in every record; the directive names the parallel layout |
96: | CRLF script shipped from a Windows checkout (2026-07) | launcher normalises; the build writes LF |
97: | silent CPU fallback (2026-06) | device assertion at preflight and in the engine check |
98: | numpy or torch ABI break from a pip upgrade (2026-08) | pin per `frozen/remote_run.sh`; never upgrade the preinstalled torch |
99: | pip resolver replacing the CUDA torch | install only pure-python packages, never torch |
100: | dropped SSH killing the job | the launcher's setsid and marker poll; the build never relies on the session |
101: | results written outside the fetched directory | one output root; the summary lists every file written |
102: | guard reads a constant instead of the environment | selftest plants a different `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` and checks the arithmetic follows it |
103: | the directive contradicts itself (m3 build 1, m4 build 3) | selftest case on the directive's numbers; on contradiction stop and report, never choose |
104: | apt lock held by unattended upgrades at boot | wait loop on the lock with a cap, then exit 2 |
105: | disk full during download or compile | free-space check at preflight against the directive's estimate |
106: | long phase with no output line | periodic progress line; the launcher's poll shows the tail |
107: | teardown not confirmed (2026-06) | launcher's retry loop; the build never terminates the box itself |
108: 
109: ## 9. What the build returns
110: 
111: `runner_py` and `onbox_sh` as paths; `selftest_output` verbatim; `onbox_command` as the single line the operator runs
112: through `remote_run_<tag>.sh`; `expected`: a table of phases with projected wall-clock from the design's numbers and
113: the record files each writes, so the reviewer can check the projection against the caps before launch.

(End of file - total 113 lines)
</content>

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Remote bootstrap for the welfare_probe Lambda box. Idempotent (marker .setup_ready), then execs
3: # whatever job command it is handed.
4: #
5: # WHY THIS DOES NOT BUILD A VENV WITH A PINNED TORCH. The sibling project's runner installs torch
6: # from the cu124 index into a plain venv, because on its 2026-06 image the default PyPI torch
7: # resolved too new for the driver and the run silently fell back to CPU. That pin is now the
8: # failure rather than the fix: measured on this image (2026-08-14, gpu_1x_a100_sxm4),
9: #
10: #     Python 3.10.12 | driver 570.148.08 | CUDA 12.8 | preinstalled torch 2.7.0+cu128, cuda True
11: #
12: # there is no cu124 wheel set that resolves, and the install dies with ResolutionImpossible before
13: # a single model is pulled. The image already ships a working CUDA torch, so the right move is to
14: # USE it and add only the missing pure-Python packages on top.
15: #
16: # transformers and accelerate are installed WITH their dependencies. Neither declares a dependency
17: # on torch, so the resolver cannot replace the working CUDA build with a CPU wheel -- which is the
18: # only way the documented "silent CPU fallback" trap could bite here. Installing --no-deps would
19: # trade that non-risk for a real one (a missing transitive dep failing mid-run, after the model
20: # download). The assertion below is what actually guards the outcome either way.
21: #
22: # The CUDA assertion is the load-bearing part and is re-run on EVERY call, warm or cold: a silent
23: # CPU fallback would bill GPU hours to produce CPU numbers that look identical in the artifact.
24: #
25: #   usage:  HF_TOKEN=hf_... bash remote_run.sh bash onbox_h1.sh
26: set -euo pipefail
27: cd ~/mats_manifold  # ADAPTED for mats_manifold: this line only; everything else byte-identical to welfare_probe/remote_run.sh
28: 
29: if [ ! -f .setup_ready ]; then
30:   echo "[setup] using preinstalled torch; adding transformers/accelerate/scikit-learn"
31:   python3 -m pip install -q --upgrade pip || true
32:   # --upgrade is load-bearing, and so is naming pillow and numpy explicitly. The image ships
33:   # numpy 1.21.5, scikit-learn 0.23.2 and a pre-9.1 Pillow in /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages;
34:   # they satisfy transformers' loose pins, so a plain install leaves them in place and the run
35:   # dies deep in an import chain -- measured, 2026-08-14:
36:   #   AttributeError: module 'PIL.Image' has no attribute 'Resampling'
37:   #     -> ModuleNotFoundError: Could not import module 'Gemma2ForCausalLM'
38:   # transformers reaches PIL through its object-detection loss module, so an image dependency
39:   # breaks a text-only run. --user installs land in ~/.local, which precedes dist-packages on
40:   # sys.path, so upgrading here shadows the stale system copies without touching the image.
41:   # numpy is PINNED to the last 1.x, not upgraded. The preinstalled torch 2.7.0 is built against
42:   # the numpy 1.x C ABI, so pulling numpy 2.x breaks it -- measured, 2026-08-14:
43:   #   AttributeError: _ARRAY_API not found / ImportError: numpy.core.multiarray failed to import
44:   # This is the numpy ABI trap the sibling project documented, reached from the other direction:
45:   # there by installing numpy too late, here by installing it too new. 1.26.4 is new enough for
46:   # current scikit-learn and transformers and old enough to keep torch's ABI intact.
47:   python3 -m pip install -q --upgrade pillow "jinja2>=3.1" "numpy==1.26.4" scikit-learn transformers accelerate
48:   touch .setup_ready
49: fi
50: 
51: python3 - <<'PY'
52: import sys
53: try:
54:     import torch
55: except Exception as e:                       # noqa: BLE001
56:     print("[setup] FATAL: torch unimportable:", e, file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(3)
57: if not torch.cuda.is_available():
58:     print("[setup] FATAL: torch.cuda.is_available() is False -> the run would SILENTLY use CPU.",
59:           "torch:", torch.__version__, file=sys.stderr)
60:     sys.exit(3)                              # loud, non-zero: RUN_DONE records it, no results produced
61: print("[setup] torch", torch.__version__, "cuda", torch.version.cuda,
62:       "device", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
63: import numpy, sklearn, transformers, PIL, jinja2   # import-ability check (fatal if an ABI clash bit)
64: # jinja2 >= 3.1 is required by apply_chat_template, and ONLY the chat path touches it -- so a stale
65: # jinja2 lets a base run finish clean while the instruct run of the same pair dies on prompt 1.
66: # Measured 2026-08-14: image ships 3.0.3 -> "ImportError: apply_chat_template requires jinja2>=3.1.0".
67: _jv = tuple(int(x) for x in jinja2.__version__.split(".")[:2])
68: if _jv < (3, 1):
69:     print("[setup] FATAL: jinja2", jinja2.__version__, "< 3.1 -> chat templates unusable", file=sys.stderr)
70:     sys.exit(3)
71: print("[setup] transformers", transformers.__version__, "numpy", numpy.__version__,
72:       "scikit-learn", sklearn.__version__, "pillow", PIL.__version__)
73: 
74: # Resolve the CONCRETE model class, not just the package. transformers imports lazily, so
75: # `import transformers` succeeds even when the Gemma-2 module cannot load; the failure then
76: # surfaces inside from_pretrained, i.e. after the box has been paid for and the checkpoint
77: # pulled. Forcing the same lookup here turns that into a five-second setup failure.
78: from transformers.models.auto.modeling_auto import MODEL_FOR_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING_NAMES  # noqa: F401
79: from transformers.models.gemma2.modeling_gemma2 import Gemma2ForCausalLM  # noqa: F401
80: print("[setup] Gemma2ForCausalLM resolvable")
81: PY
82: 
83: # gated google/gemma-2-9b{,-it} need the HF token; the launcher passes it in the run env.
84: export HF_TOKEN="${HF_TOKEN:-}"
85: export HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN="${HF_TOKEN:-}"
86: export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
87: mkdir -p out results
88: echo "[run] $*"
89: exec "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local Lambda lifecycle for ONE box: launch -> poll -> scp code -> run on-box batch ->
# fetch results -> TERMINATE. Teardown on NORMAL completion/error is guaranteed via `trap ... EXIT`;
# a LOCAL interrupt (Ctrl-C/SIGHUP) AFTER the on-box self-destruct backstop is armed deliberately does
# NOT tear down (the run is detached and the backstop bounds billing) so a stray Ctrl-C can't kill a
# live run. The remote batch also self-kills after a hard timeout. Credentials read from
# ./.keys (LAMBDA_KEY_ONE, HF_KEY_ONE) and never echoed.
#   usage: bash lambda_run.sh <instance_type> <region> <onbox_runner.sh> <local_result_dir>
#   e.g.:  VARIANT=it bash lambda_run.sh gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 us-west-2 onbox_h1.sh results_h1_it
#
# ADAPTED FROM latent_verify/lambda_run.sh -- ONLY these five things changed; every billing-safety
# mechanism below (EXIT-trap teardown, terminate() retry loop, on_signal/BACKSTOP_ARMED, on-box
# self-destruct backstop, setsid-detached run, RUN_DONE marker poll, CRLF guard, unhealthy-box early
# aborts, criticals-first fetch ordering) is byte-for-byte the original. Each encodes a real billing
# incident -- do not "simplify" any of it.
#   1. remote working dir  latent_verify/ -> welfare_probe/  (all remote paths)
#   2. scp payload         replaced with this project's files (run_h1 + libs + grid + runner)
#   3. SSH_KEY_NAME default -> latent_verify_hal_20260721 (THIS Linux workstation's registered key;
#      the old latent_verify_helios default belongs to the Windows laptop -- docs/lambda-gpu-access.md)
#   4. VARIANT/MODEL/BATCH_SIZE added to the FORWARDED env of the detached run (see the [run] block).
#      Additive only -- setsid / </dev/null / timeout / RUN_DONE are untouched. Without it the runner
#      could never learn its cell, since the fixed scp payload ships no per-cell wrapper.
#   5. this comment block
# NOT ported: lambda_reattach.sh. .last_lambda_instance is still written and the on-box backstop still
# bounds billing, so a dead launcher only loses the FETCH -- to recover it, copy
# latent_verify/lambda_reattach.sh here and swap its remote dir to welfare_probe/.
# NOTE: welfare_probe/ is not a git checkout, so GITSHA stamps "unknown" until it becomes one.
# NOTE: ./.keys must exist in THIS directory (LAMBDA_KEY_ONE, HF_KEY_ONE) -- copy it from the
# latent_verify checkout; it is gitignored and must stay that way.
set -uo pipefail
TYPE=$1; REGION=$2; RUNNER=$3; RDIR=$4
GITSHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")   # stamped into the runner's provenance
API=https://cloud.lambda.ai/api/v1
KEY=$(grep '^LAMBDA_KEY_ONE=' .keys | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r\n')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure four cost inputs of one research plan on one rented GPU box.

WHAT THIS IS. A research plan (the "card") prices a protein-structure study.
Its price rests on four numbers nobody measured. This program measures them
once, on one rented machine, and reads each against the band the plan itself
allows. The plan's own study is not run.

THE FOUR INPUTS, in the plan's own units:

  C1  af2_h_per_run        hours of one AlphaFold-Multimer prediction call
  C2  md_ns_per_day_a100   simulated nanoseconds per day of molecular dynamics
  C3  aux_h_per_pair       hours per pair of everything that is neither of those
  C4  n_storage_gib        gibibytes written by the plan's 216-run grid

Each has a stated value and a band. A measured number inside the band is PASS,
outside is FAIL, within 10 percent of a band edge is VOID and marked marginal.
The plan also states a gate on C1 alone: at most 1 hour per run. The gate is
reported. This program never branches on it.

THE ANCHOR COMES FIRST. Before any input is measured, the program redocks a
receptor fragment onto a virus capsid fragment and compares the result with the
published structure (Protein Data Bank entry 6IHB). If that redocking misses,
every input record is written VOID and the whole run is marked not valid.

STAND-IN WORK, NOT THE PLAN'S WORK. The pairs measured here are built from
chains of that one published entry. They are not the plan's own pairs. Serial
and parallel runs here are repeats on one machine; they are not independent
checks of each other, and nothing here is a second laboratory's confirmation.

HOW TO RUN

  python3 run_m4.py --selftest                 # standard library only, no GPU, no network
  python3 run_m4.py --stage extract            # downloads, controls, anchor
  python3 run_m4.py --stage generate           # docking, AlphaFold, dynamics, storage
  python3 run_m4.py --stage endpoints          # the four decisions and the summary

Each stage reads its own saved state and can run on its own, in that order.

WHAT IT WRITES, under results_m4/out/ beside this file

  endpoint-anchor_tag-m4.json      the redocking check
  endpoint-C1_tag-m4.json ...C4    one record per input
  endpoint-control-*.json          the planted-sleep, empty-run and unit checks
  rows_<arm>_tag-m4.jsonl          one line per timed run, docking, segment, byte count
  RUN_VALID.json                   whether the run is valid, and why not
  m4_summary.json                  every record restated, with no new decision
  RUN_DONE                         the exit code
  logs/                            every tool's output, saved whole

EXIT CODES
  0 finished   2 broken machine or broken harness   3 cost or time guard stop   4 anchor miss

TWO KINDS OF BAD ENDING, KEPT APART. A broken install, download, start check or
tool is the machine failing: the run is marked not valid and every input is
written as not decided. Running out of clock or money is not: the inputs that
finished keep their decisions, the rest are written as not decided and carry
the words "incomplete run", the run stays valid, and the code is 3.
"""

# Review of build 2 (m4), execution layer

Read: EXEC_NOTE.md, GATE_COMMIT.md (Pre-authorisation, Labels), run_m4.py (all 2,737 lines), onbox_m4.sh, lambda_run_m4.sh, remote_run_m4.sh, frozen/lambda_run.sh, frozen/remote_run.sh, frozen/provenance.py, out/selftest_build2.log, out/build2_return.json. Nothing run, nothing edited.

Checks that pass: checklist 3 (record convention, run_valid in every record, anchor record, RUN_VALID.json, m4_summary.json, anchor miss voids C1 to C4), 4 (nothing reads `.keys`, no environment dump, `env.txt` names variables only), 6 launcher (differs from frozen only at the declared points; terminate retry, EXIT trap, on_signal/BACKSTOP_ARMED, backstop, setsid, RUN_DONE poll, CRLF guard, unhealthy aborts, criticals-first fetch all intact), 6 remote (only the `cd` line and the comment on it differ), 7 (log ends `selftest: PASS`, 169 of 169, plausible for the planted cases present), 8 (`bash remote_run_m4.sh bash onbox_m4.sh` is what the launcher runs with RUNNER=onbox_m4.sh).

## BLOCKING

1. **BLOCKING. A guard or ceiling stop sets run_valid false.** run_m4.py:2244-2249 (`fail_stage`) calls `set_run_invalid` for every exit code. onbox_m4.sh calls `fail ... 3` at lines 109, 125, 133, 144, 147, 152, 158-160, 170 (no time left, stage hit its ceiling, generate hit the cap), so each of those writes `run_valid: false` into RUN_VALID.json, the summary and every record written after it. EXEC_NOTE item 29 and item 27: a guard stop does not set run_valid false; it voids the unfinished inputs and exits 3. Selftest has no case for `fail_stage` or the stage flow, so it did not catch this.

2. **BLOCKING. A time-guard or ceiling stop inside generate exits 0, not 3.** run_m4.py:1573-1576 (`stage_af2` returns early), 1517-1518 (`stage_aux` breaks), 1718-1719 (`stage_md` breaks). None raises `GuardStop`; the stage returns normally (and `af2` is not added to `stages_done`), the later stages run, `stage_endpoints` runs, and `run_stages` ends in `finish(state, EXIT_OK)` at 2237-2238. EXEC_NOTE items 27 and 29: a guard stop voids the unfinished inputs and exits 3. A run that stopped on its time guard with C1 or C2 unmeasured would report exit 0 and no early-stop label, and the A2(b) relaunch condition (stopped on its time guard with inputs unmeasured) would not be recognisable from RUN_DONE.

3. **BLOCKING. A timed-out AlphaFold or MD call is treated as broken infrastructure and voids everything.** run_tool (1052-1069) turns a timeout (`code = -9`) into `ToolError`. stage_af2 (1589-1611) passes `min(stage_left, seconds_left)` as the timeout and re-raises on any failed row; stage_md (1734-1744) does the same. `run_stages` (2227-2231) then marks the run not valid and `void_unmeasured` writes all four inputs VOID, including C3 (finished) and any finished AlphaFold or MD rows, because no endpoint record exists yet. The first estimate is a planning 700 s (1563) and the build's own expected run time is 600 to 900 s against a 2,100 s ceiling, so a third run overrunning its estimate is the expected case, not a corner. EXEC_NOTE items 28 and 29: a stage that hits its ceiling stops, its unfinished inputs are VOID, finished inputs keep their decisions, run_valid is untouched, exit 3.

4. **BLOCKING. REMOTE_TIMEOUT is not forwarded to the box.** lambda_run_m4.sh:168 forwards `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR`, `BUDGET_LEFT_USD`, `INSTANCE_TYPE` but not `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (it is used only in the local `timeout $REMOTE_TIMEOUT`). EXEC_NOTE Box ("forwarded env `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR BUDGET_LEFT_USD REMOTE_TIMEOUT INSTANCE_TYPE`") and item 9. onbox_m4.sh:46 therefore always sees its default 7200. At the declared 7200 nothing changes; at any shorter launch cap (a second launch sized to the money left) the launcher kills the job at the shorter cap while the on-box guard still plans for 7200, so there is no clean stop and no void record. The header at lambda_run_m4.sh:3-5 declares only three added variables, so the omission matches the header but not the EXEC_NOTE.

5. **BLOCKING. Anchor overlap compares keys that cannot match unless the receptor chain id is "B".** run_m4.py:1408 builds `native_pairs` from `rec_atoms` carrying the entry's own chain id; the pose is re-read from a PDB (`read_pdb_atoms`, 1371) written with the receptor chain forced to "B" (1388, 1727 area, `write_pdb` chain_map). `contact_overlap` (1421) intersects (chain, resseq) keys, so any receptor chain id other than "B" gives overlap 0.0 regardless of the pose. Anchor then rests on the RMSD alternative alone. EXEC_NOTE item 21; a spurious miss is an exit 4, run_valid false, and A2 forbids relaunch after an anchor miss. The selftest tests overlap on hand-built key sets only (2387-2389), not the native-versus-pose round trip.

6. **BLOCKING. No check that the declared tools start before the expensive stages, and the install line is likely to fail late.** onbox_m4.sh:134-136 installs unpinned `colabfold[alphafold]`, `jax[cuda12]`, `openmm`, `lightdock`, then only `pip freeze`. run_m4.py:1662 requires the OpenMM CUDA platform; to the reviewer's recollection (not verified, nothing may be run) the PyPI `openmm` wheel does not carry the CUDA platform (that is `openmm[cuda12]` or conda), and a later unpinned `jax[cuda12]` can break `colabfold_batch` imports. `colabfold_batch` first starts at the AlphaFold stage (after docking) and OpenMM at the MD stage (last). A failure there is exit 2 after most of the 2 h is spent, and A2(a) only authorises a second launch for a halt before the anchor decision. EXEC_NOTE item 8 wants tool-start failures to stop the run; a version/platform smoke check in the install stage (import, `Platform.getPlatformByName("CUDA")`, `colabfold_batch --help`, `lightdock3.py --help`) would put that failure inside the install ceiling. Checklist 2: would spend money without producing a valid record.

## ADVISORY

7. **ADVISORY. HF_TOKEN reaches every subprocess.** lambda_run_m4.sh:168 (inherited from frozen) and remote_run_m4.sh:84-85 put the token in the environment; run_m4.py:1042 (`run_tool`) passes the whole environment to pip-installed tools, colabfold, lightdock and OpenMM. No download here uses it (urllib at 1081 sends no token). EXEC_NOTE item 5: `HF_TOKEN` is used by downloads only. Nothing prints it. `unset HF_TOKEN HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` at the top of onbox_m4.sh would satisfy the item.

8. **ADVISORY. Docking and analysis have no stage ceiling.** EXEC_NOTE item 28 lists install 2,000, controls and anchor 700, AlphaFold 2,100, MD 1,800, endpoints 100, margin 500 = 7,200; aux (stage_aux, up to 3 x 600 s, 1522-1523) has no slot. The build's own expected shape (aux 200 to 600 s, anchor up to 600, install up to 1,800) leaves less than the AlphaFold and MD ceilings at the top of the ranges, so C1 or C2 can miss its minimum and be VOID. The 7,200 s cap itself is held by the outer timeouts and `STOP_AT`.

9. **ADVISORY. "incomplete run" label missing.** GATE_COMMIT Labels: records from an early-stopped run are labelled "incomplete run: unmeasured inputs are VOID, not holding". run_m4.py has only `LABEL_UNMEASURED = "unmeasured, not holding"` (line 182); grep for "incomplete run" finds nothing. EXEC_NOTE item 28 names only the shorter text, which is carried.

10. **ADVISORY. "Interface backbone RMSD" is the whole receptor chain.** run_m4.py:1409 and 1423 take all N, CA, C, O of the receptor chain with no superposition, not the interface residues. Stricter than the gate's readout (item 21); the label overstates what is computed.

11. **ADVISORY. `sudo -n apt-get` does not keep DEBIAN_FRONTEND.** onbox_m4.sh:113-118 exports it inside `bash -c`, but sudo resets the environment by default. Use `sudo -n env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get ...`. Stdin is /dev/null under the launcher, so the likely effect is none.

12. **ADVISORY. Outer `timeout` stops only run_m4.py.** onbox_m4.sh:153-164 on rc 124: a running `colabfold_batch` or the OpenMM worker survives and keeps the GPU while the endpoints stage runs. The inner guard's tool timeout (`seconds_left` = stop_at minus elapsed minus 500, run_m4.py:877) also outlasts the outer kill (stop_at minus elapsed minus 600), so the outer one fires first and routes into finding 1.

13. **ADVISORY. Wheel URLs and hashes are not recorded.** EXEC_NOTE items 7 and 14: each URL and sha256 recorded. The two direct downloads are (run_m4.py:1085-1087); pip and apt packages are recorded as versions only (`pip freeze`, `package_version`).

14. **ADVISORY. Build return does not match the files.** build2_return.json says run_m4.py is 1,650 lines and onbox_m4.sh 150; the files are 2,737 and 176. The selftest log therefore may not be of the files as they stand (the log has no hash). Checklist 7: counts plausible, provenance of the log unverified.

15. **ADVISORY. Selftest does not exercise the stage flow.** `run_stages`, `fail_stage` and the stage functions' guard returns have no planted case; items 27 and 29 are tested at function level only (guard_check, void_unmeasured, decide_*). Findings 1 to 3 sit in the untested layer.
Now I will read the implementation in full and audit it against all 37 checklist items.

771:             sum(p[2] for p in points) / n)

774: def threefold_axis(chain_centroids):
775:     """The local three-fold symmetry axis of three capsid copies.
776: 
777:     The axis runs through the middle of the three chain centres, along the
778:     normal of the plane they define. Fewer than three copies: no axis.
779:     """
780:     if len(chain_centroids) < 3:
781:         return None
782:     p, q, r = chain_centroids[:3]
783:     u = (q[0] - p[0], q[1] - p[1], q[2] - p[2])
784:     v = (r[0] - p[0], r[1] - p[1], r[2] - p[2])
785:     nx = u[1] * v[2] - u[2] * v[1]
786:     ny = u[2] * v[0] - u[0] * v[2]
787:     nz = u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0]
788:     norm = math.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
789:     if norm == 0:
790:         return None
791:     mid = centroid([p, q, r])
792:     return (mid, (nx / norm, ny / norm, nz / norm))

795: def distance_to_axis(point, axis):
796:     """Perpendicular distance from a point to the axis line."""
797:     if axis is None or point is None:

800:     wx, wy, wz = point[0] - ax, point[1] - ay, point[2] - az
801:     dot = wx * dx + wy * dy + wz * dz
802:     px, py, pz = wx - dot * dx, wy - dot * dy, wz - dot * dz
803:     return math.sqrt(px * px + py * py + pz * pz)

1342: def build_pairs(atoms, target_lengths=PAIR_TARGET_LENGTHS):
1343:     """Build three stand-in complexes from the chains of the published entry.
1344: 
1345:     Each complex is one capsid slot plus the receptor chain. The receptor is
1346:     taken whole. Capsid copies are added, and the last one trimmed, until the
1347:     complex has the target number of residues. Targets are spread over the
1348:     750 to 1000 residues the plan's setting calls for.
1349:     """
1350:     chains = chains_from_atoms(atoms)
1351:     seqs = {c: chain_sequence(a) for c, a in chains.items()}
1352:     ordered = sorted(seqs.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0]))
1353:     ordered = [(c, s) for c, s in ordered if len(s) >= 20]
1354:     if len(ordered) < 2:
1355:         raise ToolError("entry has fewer than two usable protein chains")
1356:     capsid_len = len(ordered[0][1])
1357:     capsid_chains = [c for c, s in ordered if len(s) == capsid_len]
1358:     receptor_chains = [c for c, s in ordered if len(s) != capsid_len]
1359:     if not receptor_chains:
1360:         raise ToolError("entry has no second distinct chain to act as the receptor")
1361:     receptor = receptor_chains[0]
1362:     receptor_seq = seqs[receptor]
1363:     pairs = []
1364:     for i, target in enumerate(target_lengths):
1365:         slot = capsid_chains[i % len(capsid_chains)]
1366:         capsid_seq = seqs[slot]
1367:         need = target - len(receptor_seq)
1368:         if need < 1:
1369:             raise ToolError("receptor chain alone already exceeds the target length")
1370:         copies = []
1371:         while need > 0:
1372:             take = min(need, len(capsid_seq))
1373:             copies.append(capsid_seq[:take])
1374:             need -= take
1375:         total = len(receptor_seq) + sum(len(c) for c in copies)
1376:         if not (PAIR_MIN_RESIDUES <= total <= PAIR_MAX_RESIDUES):
1377:             raise ToolError("built complex of %d residues, outside 750 to 1000" % total)
1378:         pairs.append({
1379:             "pair": "pair%d" % (i + 1),
1380:             "capsid_slot_chain": slot,
1381:             "receptor_chain": receptor,
1382:             "capsid_copies": len(copies),
1383:             "chain_lengths": [len(c) for c in copies] + [len(receptor_seq)],
1384:             "total_residues": total,
1385:             "sequences": copies + [receptor_seq],
1386:             "sequence_sha256": sha256_text(":".join(copies + [receptor_seq])),
1387:         })
1388:     return pairs

2184: def is_unmeasured(value, reasons) -> bool:
2185:     """Was this input left without a measurement, rather than decided on one?
2186: 
2187:     A value that exists and met its minimum was measured, even when the band
2188:     call is VOID because it sits near an edge. A missing value, or one below
2189:     the stated minimum of finished work, was not.
2190:     """
2191:     return bool(value is None or any(r == LABEL_UNMEASURED or "below the minimum" in r
2192:                                      for r in reasons))

4: # WHAT IT DOES, in this order and no other:
5: #   1. install, downloads and a start check   declared apt and pip packages, then a check that
6: #                                             every declared tool actually starts on this machine
7: #   2. controls                               a planted 60 second sleep, an empty run, a unit print
8: #   3. anchor                                 redock the receptor onto the capsid, serial then parallel
9: #   4. docking and analysis                   per pair, which is what the auxiliary hours measure
10: #   5. AlphaFold timings                      one seed at a time across all three pairs
11: #   6. dynamics timings                       one half-nanosecond production segment per complex
12: #   7. storage                                bytes written, by artifact type
13: #   8. endpoints                              the four decisions, the summary and the markers

22: #   Broken machine: a failed install, download, start check, GPU check or a tool that exits non-zero.
23: #   Nothing is retried, patched or substituted. The run is marked not valid, every input is written
24: #   as not decided, and the code is 2 (or 4 for a missed anchor).

Use `/tmp/opencode` for temporary work outside the workspace. This directory has already been created, already exists, and is pre-approved for external directory access.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location
   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use `ls foo` to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., rm "path with spaces/file.txt")
   - Examples of proper quoting:
     - mkdir "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)
     - mkdir /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail)
     - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct)
     - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail)
   - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command.
   - Capture the output of the command.

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds. If not specified, commands will time out after 120000ms.
  - If the output exceeds 2000 lines or 51200 bytes, it will be truncated and the full output will be written to a file. You can use Read with offset/limit to read specific sections or Grep to search the full content. Do NOT use `head`, `tail`, or other truncation commands to limit output; the full output will already be captured to a file for more precise searching.

  - Avoid using Bash with the `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or when these commands are truly necessary for the task. Instead, always prefer using the dedicated tools for these commands:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT find or ls)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT grep or rg)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
    - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple bash tool calls in a single message. For example, if you need to run "git status" and "git diff", send a single message with two bash tool calls in parallel.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single Bash call with '&&' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before Bash for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.
    - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)
  - AVOID using `cd <directory> && <command>`. Use the `workdir` parameter to change directories instead.
    <good-example>
    Use workdir="/foo/bar" with command: pytest tests
    </good-example>
    <bad-example>
    cd /foo/bar && pytest tests
    </bad-example>

# Git and GitHub
- Only commit, amend, push, or create PRs when explicitly requested.
- Before committing, inspect `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log --oneline -10`; stage only intended files and never commit secrets.
- Write a concise commit message that matches the repo style.
- Do not update git config, skip hooks, use interactive `-i`, force-push, or create empty commits unless explicitly requested.
- If a commit fails or hooks reject it, fix the issue and create a new commit; do not amend the failed commit.
- Before creating a PR, inspect status, diff, remote tracking, recent commits, and the diff from the base branch.
- Review all commits included in the PR, not just the latest commit.
- Use `gh` for GitHub tasks, including PRs, issues, checks, and releases; return the PR URL when done.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files. 

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file. 
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + colon + space (e.g., `1: `). Everything after that space is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the oldString or newString.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `oldString` is not found in the file with an error "oldString not found in content".
- The edit will FAIL if `oldString` is found multiple times in the file with an error "Found multiple matches for oldString. Provide more surrounding lines in oldString to identify the correct match." Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replaceAll` to change every instance of `oldString`. 
- Use `replaceAll` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

newString.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Replace all occurrences of oldString (default false)

function.name: glob
function.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches as a batch that are potentially useful.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

function.name: grep
function.description:
- Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size
- Searches file contents using regular expressions
- Supports full regex syntax (eg. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+", etc.)
- Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (eg. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")
- Returns file paths and line numbers with matching lines
- Use this tool when you need to find files containing specific patterns
- If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`.
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: File pattern to include in the search (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file or directory from the local filesystem. If the path does not exist, an error is returned.

Usage:
- The filePath parameter should be an absolute path.
- By default, this tool returns up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- The offset parameter is the line number to start from (1-indexed).
- To read later sections, call this tool again with a larger offset.
- Use the grep tool to find specific content in large files or files with long lines.
- If you are unsure of the correct file path, use the glob tool to look up filenames by glob pattern.
- Contents are returned with each line prefixed by its line number as `<line>: <content>`. For example, if a file has contents "foo\n", you will receive "1: foo\n". For directories, entries are returned one per line (without line numbers) with a trailing `/` for subdirectories.
- Any line longer than 2000 characters is truncated.
- Call this tool in parallel when you know there are multiple files you want to read.
- Avoid tiny repeated slices (30 line chunks). If you need more context, read a larger window.
- This tool can read image files and PDFs and return them as file attachments.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file or directory to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines to read (defaults to 2000)

function.name: write

Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

content.description: The content to write to the file

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)
